q1_insightface.channel: Commercial model licensing is sold as a separate product from MIT code. Primary channels: (1) recognition-oss-pack@insightface.ai for open-source face recognition packs (explicitly including buffalo_l); (2) contact@insightface.ai for InspireFace SDK, inswapper, proprietary models, and general enterprise; (3) web form at insightface.ai/contact (use-case dropdown includes 'Face Recognition Model Licensing'; business email required). Maintainer nttstar (Jia Guo) directs pricing questions to contact@insightface.ai. No public price list, self-serve cart, or published quote bands found as of 2026-07-23.
q1_insightface.entity: InsightFace AI Technology Limited (legal/publisher entity on insightface.ai; © 2026). Project primarily maintained by Jia Guo (guojia@insightface.ai / nttstar) and Jiankang Deng. DeepGlint is a historical research collaborator (e.g., Partial FC / Glint360K training-set releases ~2020), NOT the commercial licensor for buffalo_* packs today. Consumer product brand Picsi.ai is operated by the same InsightFace ecosystem. Tracxn lists InsightFace as founded ~2019, unfunded.
q1_insightface.covers_model_zoo: YES for open-source model packages: official commercial page explicitly lists commercial usage rights for buffalo_l, antelopev2, buffalo_s, buffalo_m, etc. Separate SKUs exist for (a) OSS model pack commercial license, (b) closed-source higher-accuracy proprietary models, (c) InspireFace C/C++ SDK, (d) inswapper face-swap models. Commercial deliverable for recognition is ONNX model files for offline self-hosted inference (not a long-term hosted dependency). Code remains MIT free; pretrained weights remain non-commercial without a paid grant. No public evidence of OEM/reseller price sheets; site claims '40+ international enterprise partners' without naming resellers.

summary_for_decision: DECISION THIS WEEK: (1) InsightFace commercial path is real and explicitly covers buffalo_l model packs via recognition-oss-pack@insightface.ai / contact@insightface.ai under InsightFace AI Technology Limited—but there is genuinely zero public pricing; email with company domain immediately. Code=MIT, weights=NC without license; commercial SKU is the model zoo rights (ONNX offline), not only an SDK. DeepGlint is historical research collab, not the licensor. (2) Detector gap is the product risk: YuNet is clean (MIT/BSD) but weak on masks (user 0.321); buffalo/RetinaFace-SCRFD-class detectors are strong but InsightFace pretrained weights are NC. SCRFD code is Apache-2.0 yet InsightFace .onnx weights are still NC—do not ship them without a license or a clean retrain. Avoid YOLOv5-face (GPL-3) and Ultralytics (AGPL-3) for proprietary SaaS. (3) Clean-weight recognition beyond SFace: AuraFace-v1 (Apache-2.0) is the main commercially marketed open embedder; pair with a clean detector. Synthetic stacks (IDiff-Face NC; DCFace unclear license; Vec2Face MIT but ships Glint360K auxiliaries) are not a one-week production fix. (4) Among commercial SDKs that small SaaS can actually buy: Neurotechnology VeriLook is uniquely self-serve with public €339/€859 SDK + per-server component euros and ARM Linux—default buy shortlist for CPU/ARM. Luxand FaceSDK is trial+quote, ARM-friendly, mask-on detection marketed. CyberLink FaceMe and ROC are capable (NIST-participating, mask claims/history, ARM/edge) but sales-quoted. Paravision/Innovatrics/Corsight/NEC/Idemia/Oosto/Trueface are enterprise/surveillance—poor low-touch fit. (5) Recommended parallel moves: email InsightFace for buffalo_l quote; order VeriLook Extended trial and bench DETECTION on the private 150-image mask subset; A/B YuNet vs MediaPipe full-range vs (if licensed) buffalo detector on ARM A1 latency; keep SFace/AuraFace as clean embedders. Prefer licensing buffalo detector (or whole pack) over hoping a permissive detector matches 0.865 masked recovery without retrain.
